clue.text: Slave girl taken back by Virginia

parts.note: VA is the standard abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

indicators.note: taken back says the girl's word is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl

explanation.surface: A slave girl is carried off home to Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken back' reverses the girl; a vassal was a feudal dependant bound to a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: A vassal was a feudal subordinate, so the word serves as a synonym for a slave or servile dependant.

clue.text: Strong, virile types apparently held in check

indicators.note: held in means kept inside, so the men go inside the check

parts.note: to vet is to check
he-men are macho, virile men

explanation.surface: Powerful macho men are seemingly restrained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' only softens the surface; 'held in' puts the macho men inside the check.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement means forceful or intense, as in a strong objection.

clue.text: Person not remembered as a difficult customer

definitions.meaning: a placeholder for someone whose name one has forgotten
an unpleasant or awkward person, used euphemistically

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase stands in for a forgotten name and is also a polite word for a nasty person.

clue.text: Adoption may be moving

definitions.meaning: assuming or putting on a manner, as in feigning an accent

explanation.definitionFit: Affecting a manner means adopting it artificially; an affecting scene is touching or moving.

clue.text: Drunk ranting about nothing in the dark

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go round the zero
drunk suggests the letters of ranting are reeling about out of order

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A drunk rants without making any sense, as if lost in darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' makes IGNRANT from RANTING; 'about' puts it around O.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the dark is an idiom for lacking knowledge, which is what being uninformed means.

clue.text: Persuade defensive team-mate to even the score?

parts.note: to get someone to do something is to persuade them
a back on your own side, a defender, is one's own back

explanation.surface: A player talks a defender into helping level the match.
explanation.walkthrough: In football or rugby a back is a defensive player.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to take revenge, to settle a score with someone who wronged you.

clue.text: Half the Tories may go to see colleagues elsewhere

indicators.note: half signals that only the first five of the ten letters are used

parts.note: when this puzzle appeared Labour governed Britain, so the Tories were the Opposition

explanation.surface: Some Conservatives might visit their counterparts abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tories were then the Opposition; its first half gives OPPOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppos is informal for opposite numbers, people doing the same job in another organisation.

clue.text: Bag containing a hundred and twenty-five pieces of paper

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a quire is 24 or 25 sheets of writing paper

explanation.surface: A sack holds a stack of 125 sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bag' is a verb, to get hold of; 'containing' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To bag something is informal for getting or obtaining it.

clue.text: Guess what turned up in politician's possession?

indicators.note: in, with possession, places the reversed word inside

parts.note: a Tory is a Conservative politician

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: eh? is a way of saying what?

explanation.surface: Try guessing what a politician has been found holding.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' means read bottom to top; 'in' with 'possession' places that inside the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a supposition or conjecture, which is what a guess is.

clue.text: Nice phrase for the very best

definitions.text: Nice phrase for the very best

parts.words: Nice phrase for the very best
parts.note: Nice is the French city, so this asks for a French expression meaning the elite

explanation.definitionFit: This French expression, literally 'cream of the cream', means the pick of the bunch, the elite.

clue.text: I fret and dash off without thinking enough

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone off course and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worrier rushes away before thinking things through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' only joins the two fodder pieces; 'off' rearranges IFRETDASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something headlong, plunging in recklessly, is acting rashly and without due thought.

clue.text: Needle caused game to finish early

indicators.note: finishing early means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: piquet is a card game for two players

explanation.surface: Someone was annoyed when a game was cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: PIQUET, an old card game, loses its last letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to irritate them, and as a verb pique also means to irritate or nettle.

clue.text: Many hate having to accept Conservative's suggestion

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a crossword shorthand for many

indicators.note: to accept means to take something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: odium means hatred
C abbreviates Conservative

explanation.surface: Many people hate it when they must go along with a Tory's proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having to accept' puts C into ODIUM, giving ODICUM after M.
explanation.definitionFit: A modicum is a small amount, and a suggestion can mean a slight trace or hint of something.

clue.text: Point when row becomes more unpleasant

parts.note: N, north, is a compass point
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: An argument turns nastier the moment someone makes a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' tempts as a quarrel but is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of nasty means more disagreeable or offensive.

clue.text: I grumble about mother-in-law

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the whole phrase is read backwards

parts.note: to moan is to grumble

explanation.surface: Someone complains about their wife's or husband's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns IMOAN round. In the Bible, Naomi is Ruth's mother-in-law.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Ruth, Naomi is the mother of Ruth's late husband, the Bible's best-known mother-in-law.

clue.text: Recalled colourful chap hanging round soldiers in the mess

indicators.note: hanging round means surrounding the soldiers
recalled means called back, so the two words run backwards

parts.note: red is a colour
Sid is a man's name, standing for any chap
OR, other ranks, means soldiers

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a flamboyant fellow loitering near troops in the canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' turns REDSID into DISDER, which goes round OR. 'mess' looks like a military dining hall but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is a state of chaos or untidiness, the same thing as confusion.

clue.text: Forgiving the Queen over official letter

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
a missive is an official letter

explanation.surface: The monarch is lenient about a formal message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns ER into RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Remissive means remitting or pardoning, hence forgiving.

clue.text: Broadcast star can't handle

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A celebrity on air cannot cope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' rearranges STARCANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To transact business is to conduct or handle it.

clue.text: Bribe to get a flat or house

parts.note: a bung is British slang for a bribe
flat land is low-lying

explanation.surface: Someone pays a bribe to secure an apartment or home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment but is the adjective low. BUNG is British slang for a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungalow is a one-storey dwelling, a type of house.

clue.text: Funny tour involving funny artist

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the scrambled letters surround the illness
funny means odd, so the letters are arranged oddly

parts.note: taken as written
feeling funny means unwell, ill

explanation.surface: An amusing trip features a comic painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' appears twice with two jobs: first an anagram signal, then meaning unwell; 'involving' sets the second inside. Maurice Utrillo painted Paris street scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Utrillo was a French painter, known for Montmartre streetscapes.

clue.text: Main difficulty, after retirement, facing men

indicators.note: retirement means withdrawal, going back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to be in a jam is to be in difficulty
OR, other ranks, means soldiers or men

explanation.surface: The chief problem in retiring is having to face other people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after retirement' reads like a pensioner's life but signals a reversal of the difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Major means chief or principal, as in a major road or main road.

clue.text: Fit of depression's a habit for some when retired

definitions.meaning: a fit of nerves or low spirits

definitions.text: a habit for some when retired
definitions.meaning: pyjamas, the clothing some wear after going to bed

explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang both for a bout of jitters or gloom and for nightwear worn in bed.

clue.text: Moan about story ultimately lacking in conviction

indicators.note: about means around, so the complaint surrounds the shortened story

parts.note: beef is slang for a complaint or moan

indicators.note: ultimately lacking means the last letter is missing

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a tale lacks persuasiveness in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately lacking' trims the story's last letter; 'about' wraps the complaint round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A conviction is a firmly held belief, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Inconsistent interpretation of criteria I rejected

indicators.note: an interpretation is a fresh reading, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A reading of the rules that I rejected was inconsistent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' takes I out of CRITERIA; the remaining CRTERIA is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means irregular and unpredictable, so it serves as a synonym for inconsistent.

clue.text: Hear about a con, maybe?

parts.note: a judge tries, or hears, a case
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A court is asked to consider whether a swindle took place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' is the judge's sense, to try a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A try-on is British slang for an attempt to deceive, and a con is one example.

clue.text: Key union facilitator represented worst staff

parts.note: to worst someone is to beat them, the same as to best them
to staff is to man, provide with workers

explanation.surface: A key figure in a trade union represented the poorest employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' is a marriage, not a trade union; 'worst' and 'staff' are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: At a wedding the groomsman in chief helps the marriage go smoothly, a playful description of that role.

clue.text: One do in part of the Hebrides

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to do someone in can be to kill them, or slay

explanation.surface: A party is held on one of the Scottish islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' looks like a party but is the verb slay. Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Islay is one of the islands of the Inner Hebrides, so it is a part of that group.

clue.text: A Chilean dish originally mistaken for a Mexican one

indicators.note: mistaken suggests the letters are taken wrongly, in a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of dish

explanation.surface: A South American plate is confused with one from Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistaken' rearranges ACHILEAN plus D, the first letter of dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The enchilada is a rolled, filled tortilla from Mexico, so it is a Mexican dish.

clue.text: Be out of one's depth as a swimmer?

definitions.meaning: to struggle helplessly, unable to cope
a flatfish, a creature that swims

explanation.surface: Someone out of their depth is a poor swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: To struggle clumsily is one sense; the other is the flatfish, a swimmer in the sea.

clue.text: Cheap digs sought in county one time

parts.note: Beds is the abbreviation for Bedfordshire, an English county
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone once looked for cheap lodgings in the shires.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedfordshire is a county north of London, shortened to Beds.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsit is a single rented room for living and sleeping, cheap lodgings, which British slang calls digs.
